shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: shadow-sm, shadow, shadow-md, shadow-lg are deliberately none; the system is flat.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Two-ring focus indicator on tabs and custom controls; elsewhere a 2px outline offset 2px.

shadows.name: mini-board-frame

shadows.name: board-square-ring
shadows.purpose: Square highlight rings on the chessboard (error, success, warning, accent).

motion.name: transition
motion.purpose: Default hover and colour transitions on buttons, tabs, inputs.

motion.name: chart-grow
motion.purpose: Trend bars growing in; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Ranked bars stack; trend values shrink; chart gutter narrows.

breakpoints.name: drawer-sheet
breakpoints.purpose: Side drawer becomes a bottom sheet.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.purpose: Trend spine and trainer collapse to one column.

theming.model: Every semantic token is light-dark(<light>, <dark>). Light values read --user-* custom properties first, written at runtime from the user's saved theme (DEFAULT_THEME / THEME_PRESETS in blunder_tutor/web/api/_settings_schemas.py); dark values are fixed. color-scheme follows data-theme (light/dark) or prefers-color-scheme. Board colours and piece sets are a separate subsystem with their own presets.

accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA target; dashboard text uses contrast-checked --color-dashboard-* tokens.
Every chart ships an sr-only data table.
2px focus outline offset 2px on all focusable elements.
44px minimum hit areas under pointer: coarse.
Reduced-motion fallbacks for chart and trainer animation.
Better/worse is always stated in words, not colour alone.

narrative.overview:
Blunder Tutor reads like a chess player's own scoresheet after a bad game: warm paper, black ink, heavy rules between sections, and a few marks in colour where something went right or wrong. The ground is a warm off-white in light mode and a warm near-black in dark mode; everything structural is drawn in ink (or its dark-mode inversion) with flat fills and square corners. There are no drop shadows, no gradients, no rounded cards. Depth comes from rules and inversion, never from lift.

Density is that of a working document, not a marketing page. One element owns each view: on the dashboard a single trend chart with a sentence-case verdict above it; in the trainer the board, kept whole, with the result laid beside it as two mini boards. Everything else is ranked under that owner with ink weight and opacity rather than with extra colour. Colour is reserved for meaning: green says better or best, red says worse or your miss, yellow marks the one action you should take next.

The system descends from a Bauhaus token set (the source still names it that), and the primary triad survives in the tokens. The newest surfaces have narrowed it: blue has retreated to links, focus and informational states, and charts are ink.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, ink text and ink charts; dark mode is the same world inverted, not a new palette.
3px ink rules divide sections and frame boards; 2px ink strokes outline controls.
Jost uppercase for small labels, tabs, buttons and nav; Jost sentence case for display headings and verdicts; DM Sans for body and numbers.
Colour carries meaning only: green better, red worse, yellow the single primary action.
Charts are hand-drawn in HTML/SVG with ink bars, reference lines and a screen-reader table; no chart library.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green only ever means better or best; red only ever means worse or your miss; yellow only ever means the action to take. A colour that means something on one chart may not mean something else on the next.

rules.name: The Ink For Volume Rule
rules.body: Counts, shares and frequencies are drawn in ink at stepped opacity or along the ink ramp (heatmap levels, ranked bars, games-played strips). Hue is never used to encode volume.

rules.name: The Single Highlight Rule
rules.body: Within one breakdown, exactly one row may be drawn at full ink (the leader); the rest sit at about 35% ink, and rows resting on too little data (fewer than 10 games) drop to about 15% and muted text and are never the highlight.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: A view carries one yellow button. Secondary actions are ink-outlined.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Uppercase Jost is for naming things (labels, controls, containers). Statements meant to be read as sentences (verdicts, section headings, result headlines) are sentence case. Never set a sentence in caps.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can be compared with another number uses tabular figures: chart axes, trend values, side-column values, ranked-bar values, library status.

rules.name: The Owner Rule
rules.body: Each view has one element that owns the first viewport (the trend, the board). Everything else is visibly subordinate to it.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Surfaces do not cast shadows; if something needs separating, draw a rule.

dos: **Do** separate sections with a 3px ink rule and outline controls with 2px ink.
**Do** draw new charts in ink with reference lines, a baseline, tabular axis labels and an sr-only data table, using no third-party chart library.
**Do** give each breakdown exactly one full-ink highlight and mute rows with fewer than 10 games behind it.
**Do** use one yellow primary button per view and ink outlines for everything else.
**Do** set statements in sentence-case Jost and names of things in uppercase Jost labels.
**Do** route every colour through the light-dark() tokens so dark mode and user themes follow.
**Do** meet WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast-checked dashboard text colours, visible 2px focus outlines, 44px touch targets on coarse pointers, reduced-motion fallbacks.
donts: **Don't** add drop shadows, glows or gradients; the shadow tokens are none on purpose.
**Don't** round corners on cards, buttons, inputs, tabs or charts.
**Don't** encode volume or rank with hue; use the ink ramp or ink opacity.
**Don't** use green, red or yellow for anything other than better, worse and the primary action.
**Don't** cover the board with the trainer result; it belongs beside the board.
